text.p: A top security adviser to Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma on Wednesday hailed the re-election of U.S. President Bill Clinton and praised him for improving relations between Kiev and Washington in his first term.
"During President Clinton's rule we significantly improved Ukrainian-U.S. relations," Volodymyr Horbulin, secretary of the powerful Security and Defence Council, told reporters.

Horbulin also said that Kuchma had sent a congratulatory telegram to Clinton, who soundly defeated Republican challenger Bob Dole on Tuesday to become the first Democrat re-elected to the White House since Franklin Roosevelt in 1944.

"We have a much better mutual understanding with the United States on the future of Europe's security structure," he added, apparently referring to Ukraine's close relationship with the NATO Western alliance.

Ukraine's relations with Washington were strained at first after it won independence from the Kremlin in 1991 -- until Kiev agreed in 1994 to get rid of more than 1,800 nuclear warheads, inherited from the former Soviet superpower.
Kiev is the third largest recipient of U.S. financial aid after Egypt and Israel, with Washington allocating $330 million in grants and $650 million in credits this year.
A Ukrainian-U.S. body, headed by Kuchma and Vice-President Al Gore, was set up last September to deal with security, foreign policy, economy and investment, and called the Kuchma-Gore Commission.
"I was very worried before the election that we might have to change the name of the Commission," Horbulin joked.
